messages:
Anya (PM): Sharing the initial RFC draft for Structured Output & Tool/Function Calling. Focus: schema design, validation flow, and graceful error handling. Looking for acceptance criteria and obvious missing edge cases. Link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/so-fn-calling-draft :eyes:

Marc (Eng): skimmed. high-level looks good. can we be explicit about who owns runtime validation vs caller-side?

Anya (PM): good q. Proposal: runtime (server-side) must validate output against the schema as a safety net; callers are strongly encouraged to validate before sending tool outputs back into the system. Acceptance criterion: runtime rejects nonconforming outputs and emits structured errors with codes so clients can auto-retry or fallback.

Sasha (ML): also want a note on ambiguous model outputs. sometimes model emits partial JSON or extra fields. acceptance criteria should include lenient/strict modes. maybe default = lenient with warnings logged, strict for enterprise customers.

Jordan (DevEx): +1 on lenient/strict toggle. Dev experience note: add example SDK error handling snippet and a way to surface validation warnings in the console UI.

Marc (Eng): technical edge: KV-cache + streaming tokens. if model outputs streaming JSON, we need incremental parsing strategy. RFC should define how partial JSON fragments map to validation and when to abort.

Anya (PM): added incremental parsing section: runtime will attempt streaming parse; if partial parse succeeds into a stable prefix, it can emit partial tooling calls (with a flag). If parse stalls or never completes by a timeout, emit ERROR_PARTIAL_PARSE with context. Acceptance: timeout and error codes defined.

Kevin (SRE): SLA/observability: we need latency budgets for validation step (default 5ms median, 20ms p95 per call) otherwise validation becomes bottleneck. Also require structured logs with query_id, model_variant, schema_id.

Marc (Eng): for schema format we propose compact JSON Schema subset plus annotations for 'callable' fields and 'security' metadata. sample in RFC: ```
{"type":"object","properties":{"action":{"type":"string","callable":true},"args":{"type":"object"}},"required":["action"]}
```

Sasha (ML): edge case: model hallucination returns a callable name that doesn't exist. runtime should map to ERROR_UNKNOWN_TOOL and include similarity suggestions (top-3 matching tool names). Acceptance: include similarity heuristic > 0.7 confidence => suggest auto-map optional.

Jordan (DevEx): SDK ergonomics: show this example for retry/backoff: ```js
try { await client.callTool(response); } catch (e) { if (e.code==='ERROR_PARTIAL_PARSE') { // surface to user and allow manual edit } if (e.code==='ERROR_UNKNOWN_TOOL') { // show suggestions: e.suggestions } }```

Anya (PM): good snippets. Next: launch criteria. Must have: schema versioning docs, validation error spec, streaming parse behavior, SDK examples, console warnings, and 3 customer sign-offs (two early-adopter customers + platform).

Kevin (SRE): add chaos test: simulate high-rate malformed outputs and verify validation circuit-breaker trips and alerts. Acceptance: no P50 latency regression >10% for unrelated endpoints.

Marc (Eng): can we define error codes list in RFC? I'll draft that section: ERROR_PARTIAL_PARSE, ERROR_SCHEMA_VIOLATION, ERROR_UNKNOWN_TOOL, ERROR_AUTHZ, ERROR_TIMEOUT, ERROR_INTERNAL_VALIDATION.

Sasha (ML): also add a note on evaluation: tie quality regressions to prompts/evals and alert when schema-conformance drop > 5% over baseline.

Anya (PM): thanks all. Action items: Marc -> detailed error codes + streaming parse design; Jordan -> SDK examples + console flows; Kevin -> observability & chaos tests; Sasha -> eval criteria + lenient/strict behavior examples. I'll update PRD with these acceptance criteria and ping for final review by EOD Monday. :calendar: :rocket:
